correctness.rationale: Every even r=2s>=2 is covered by a full orthogonal invariant decomposition: the twin difference eigenline at 2, an s-dimensional antisymmetric irreducible Jacobi block, and an (s+2)-dimensional symmetric irreducible Jacobi block. Their determinant formulas are reconstructed from correct normalized weights 2 and sqrt2. A common root forces t=plus or minus 2, but neither value annihilates the odd-sector continuant. Thus only eigenvalue 2 can repeat, exactly if s odd. Bipartite diagonal similarity gives Q spectra. A direct distance-pair argument resolves r>=6 and all two-vertex choices fail for r2,4. Exact SymPy polynomial and BFS checks for r=2,4,...,24 replayed successfully; finite computations are secondary to the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The motivating primary paper expressly poses theta-graph equality as an open classification direction and proves only odd theta arms. Completing the even branch yields an infinite simultaneous equality family (r=4j+2, j>=1), a separate infinite simple-spectrum family (r=4j,j>=1), and precisely identified short exceptions. The new all-eigenvalue simplicity argument is a nontrivial necessary step not supplied by the known eigenvalue-two inertia count. The result gives an exact natural spectral/metric boundary, not a routine isolated substitution.
